items.title: Supreme Court dismisses plea for recitation of Preamble during morning assembly in schools
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday dismissed a public interest litigation (PIL) seeking directions to formulate a national policy mandating the daily recitation of the Preamble to the Constitution during morning assemblies in schools nationwide [Dheeraj Kumar v. Union of India & Anr]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Augustine George Masih refused to entertain the plea, remarking that the Preamble is already part of the foundational school curriculum and is taught to students across the country from Class 6 onwards. Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Sandeep Mehta and Justice Augustine George Masih The PIL was instituted by Dheeraj Kumar, an Assistant Professor at Rajdhani College, Delhi University, through Advocate-on-Record Rohit Kumar. The petitioner sought a writ of mandamus directing the Union Ministry of Education and the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) to frame a nationwide policy framework to promote constitutional literacy among school students. items.title: ‘A civilisational crisis’: The IISc professor whose AI talk went viral
items.summary: Study maths, learn to think, learn programming or get a job. For a generation of Indian STEM students, that was the script. Now AI may be tearing up that playbook – so how do we adapt to this new world order?. In this conversation, Indulekha Aravind speaks with Dr Prathosh AP, assistant professor in the Department of Electrical Communication Engineering at IISc Bengaluru, whose classroom talk on pedagogy in the age of AI went viral. If our only goal is to improve efficiency and productivity, why work with humans, with our quirks and limitations – why not use AI, rather than people, he asks. What is our “moat”, as humans? What will become of work, as we know it, and the process of learning? Would there be any point in having colleges, classrooms and lectures? And are we having enough conversations about this "civilisational shift” that’s under way? Three of Prathosh’s students, who were in his class the day of his viral lecture and whose questions, in fact, provoked that talk, join him in the studio to explain their anxieties and hopes in this changing world. Prathosh also explains why his inbox flooded, and why he couldn’t sleep. Watch the full conversation. A quarter-century of Mo

items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Tuesday issued a contempt of court notice to Chief Secretary KP Sinha for misrepresenting facts about the filing of Punjab government's appeal before the Supreme Court against the High Court's recent order for payment of pending dearness allowance (DA) to government employees. On August 3, the High Court had directed the State to release all up-to-date pending installments of dearness allowance/dearness relief (DA/DR) to all its employees and pensioners, respectively, at the same rates as paid to the All India Services (IAS/IPS/IFS) officers serving within Punjab. The judgment, which also bars the government from resorting to any unproductive expenditures such as large-scale advertising campaigns in print or social media till non-payment of the dues, has been challenged by the State before the Supreme Court. However, the appeal has been before the top court Registry since September 1, owing to defects. On Tuesday, the High Court had sought a report from the Supreme Court Registry about the status of the SLP moved by the State.
